title: GitLab warns of max severity code execution vulnerability
content_md: GitLab warned users today to immediately patch a maximum-severity vulnerability in the CI/CD Regular Expression Compiler that could let remote attackers run arbitrary code on targeted instances. Tracked as CVE-2026-97229 , this critical security flaw was discovered by a security researcher using the ' joaxcar ' handle and reported via GitLab's HackerOne bug bounty program. CVE-2026-97229 stems from an integer overflow weakness in GitLab's CI/CD Regular Expression Compiler, which parses, compiles, and evaluates regular expressions in projects' pipeline configuration files. "GitLab has remediated an issue that, under certain conditions, could have allowed an unauthenticated user to execute arbitrary code on the GitLab server via a specially crafted regular expression in a CI/CD configuration, due to insufficient regular expression validation," the company explained in a Monday advisory. GitLab fixed the security issue in GitLab Community Edition (CE) and Enterprise Edition (EE) versions from 19.2 before 19.2.8, 19.3 before 19.3.4, and 19.4 before 19.4.2, and urged users to patch their servers immediately. "These versions contain important bug and security fixes, and we strongly recommend that all self-managed GitLab installations be upgraded to one of these versions immediately," it warned.
